column1: # Which rubric rows each cutover probe covers, and which rows are deliberately
# not probed. Tab-separated; lines starting with # are comments.
# WHY THIS IS DATA AND NOT SHELL. Two reasons, and the second is the one that
# matters. Adding a probe should be a table edit, not a code edit — and rubric
# row identifiers are milestone identifiers, which RULE TST-NAM bars from
# source. The same split `docs/metrics.census.tsv` makes for metric families:
# the contract is data the code is graded against, never a literal inside it.
#   milestone <id>                    a merged milestone whose rubric rows must be covered
#   covers    <probe name>            space-separated rows; `*` expands to every milestone
#   exclude   <milestone:row>         the reason it is deliberately not probed
# THE S-LETTERS DRIFTED, so hygiene rows below are enumerated rather than
# wildcarded. `*` expands by LETTER (probes.sh expand_rows), which was safe
# while every milestone used the same six-row tail. M181_003 and M181_004 put
# the integration lane at S3 and pushed lint, version and secrets down one, so
# `covers lint *:S3` would have tagged the lint probe onto an integration row —
# covered on paper, proven by the wrong command. Only S1 and S2 still agree
# across all eleven and still use the wildcard.
# The durable fix is to key hygiene rows by MEANING rather than letter, which
# is a probes.sh schema change; it is named in M181_006's Discovery rather than
# made here, because widening a green gate's code and its data in one step
# leaves nothing to bisect if the result is red.
